text.linkedin:
The EU just delayed the hard part of AI regulation. One piece of it didn't move.

On 29 June 2026, the EU Council adopted the "Digital Omnibus on AI," pushing back the high-risk AI obligations (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Articles 8–17):

→ Standalone high-risk systems: 2 August 2026 → 2 December 2027
→ High-risk AI embedded in regulated products: → 2 August 2028

What still lands on 2 August 2026, unchanged: Article 50's transparency rules. Disclose that someone's talking to AI. Label deepfakes and synthetic content. Mark generated output as machine-made, with a grace period to December 2026 for systems already live.

The postponement isn't a cancellation. The obligations in Articles 8–17 are unchanged, only the dates moved.

Here's the part I'd act on either way: every one of those delayed obligations (risk management, human oversight, technical documentation) describes a control you'd want before the deadline forces it, not after.

A rule like this doesn't wait for 2027:

when an agent's output reaches a customer or the public, a human reviews it first.

Regulation moves on its own schedule. The actions it's asking for don't have to.

Sources: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; Digital Omnibus on AI, adopted 29 June 2026.

#AIGovernance #EUAIAct #Compliance
